# Temple Scroll Column 47 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 47 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**47:1** If she becomes married while her vows or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself are still in effect —

**47:2** and her husband hears and remains silent on the day he learns of them — her vows shall stand, and her binding obligations shall remain in force.

**47:3** But if her husband annuls them on the day he learns of them, the LORD will pardon her.

**47:4** The vow of a widow or a divorced woman — everything by which she has bound herself shall be binding upon her.

**47:5** These are the statutes the LORD commanded concerning vows between a husband and his wife, and between a father and his daughter during her youth in her father's house.

**47:6** When a man or a woman consecrates a special vow — the vow of a Nazirite — to dedicate himself to the LORD,

**47:7** he shall abstain from wine and fermented drink; he shall not consume vinegar made from wine or from fermented drink, nor shall he drink any grape juice, nor eat grapes whether fresh or dried.

**47:8** Throughout the entire period of his dedication, he shall not eat anything produced from the grapevine, from seed to skin.

**47:9** Throughout the entire period of his vow of dedication, no razor shall touch his head. Until the days of his dedication to the LORD are fulfilled, he shall be holy; he shall allow the hair of his head to grow uncut.

**47:10** Throughout the entire period of his dedication to the LORD, he shall not approach a dead body.

**47:11** He shall abstain from wine and fermented drink; he shall not consume vinegar of wine or vinegar of fermented drink, nor shall he drink any grape juice.

**47:12** For his father or his mother, for his brother or his sister — he shall not defile himself when they die, for the consecration of his God is upon his head.

**47:13** Throughout the entire period of his dedication, he is holy to the LORD.

**47:14** If someone dies suddenly in his presence, thereby defiling the head of his consecration, he shall shave his head on the day of his purification — on the seventh day he shall shave it.

**47:15** On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**47:16** The priest shall offer one as a purification offering and one as a burnt offering and shall make atonement for him, because he incurred guilt through the dead body. He shall reconsecrate his head on that day.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 47 concludes vow regulations and presents the Nazirite legislation (Numbers 6:1-12). LOGOS renders shekar as "fermented drink" rather than "strong drink" for precision. The Nazirite's triple abstinence (grape products, haircutting, corpse contact) represents total consecration. "Purification offering" for chattat in v. 16 reflects the decontamination function. The accidental contamination protocol preserves the Numbers 6:9-12 procedure.*
